sources.note: Replaces uniform test-time compute allocation with a training-free agent that picks reasoning tools, a search strategy and an exploration parameter per problem, using a process reward model both to prune within a trajectory and to select across iterations.
sources.title: What If We Allocate Test-Time Compute Adaptively?

sources.note: Proves that parameterizing an outcome reward as the log-likelihood ratio between a policy and a reference model makes the per-step Q value fall out of the same model for free, so a process reward model can be obtained by training an outcome reward model on response-level labels alone.
sources.title: Free Process Rewards without Process Labels

sources.note: A systematic empirical study of entropy in RLVR that finds entropy correlates with response diversity but only weakly and inconsistently with accuracy, identifies clipping thresholds, off-policy updates and data diversity as its drivers, and argues positive-advantage tokens are what collapses it.
sources.title: Revisiting Entropy in Reinforcement Learning for Large Reasoning Models

result.definition: The instruction-tuned 8B Llama-3.1 model, used across these sources as a mid-capability workhorse rather than a subject of study. It serves as a generation model for best-of-N evaluation of reward models, as the base for training an implicit process reward model, and as one of two base models for an adaptive inference agent — where it shows the larger adaptive gain of the two (43.8 to 65.4 on MATH-500) and a distinctly different controller profile from the Qwen model, spreading tool selection across several options where Qwen concentrates on two. Note that this entry is filed as a dataset because the archived summaries listed evaluated models in the dataset field; it is a model, not a corpus.
